questions.question: Explain why the vertical interval and horizontal equivalent must be in the same units before dividing, and what happens to the answer if they are not.
questions.expected_answer: A ratio compares two quantities of the same kind; dividing metres by kilometres produces a number 1 000 times too large or small with no physical meaning. In our example, using 4,5 instead of 4 500 gives 1 : 66,7-style nonsense instead of the true 1 : 15.

questions.question: A gradient of 1 : 15 and a gradient of 1 : 150 — which is steeper and why? Explain the interpretation rule in your own words.
questions.expected_answer: 1 : 15 is steeper. The number after the colon is the horizontal distance over which you gain 1 metre of height; gaining a metre every 15 m of walking is a much sharper climb than gaining it every 150 m. The larger the second number, the gentler the slope.

questions.question: Describe the full exam layout for a gradient answer and the three verification checks you run before moving on.
questions.expected_answer: Layout: state the formula (VI/HE), substitute with both values in the same unit (300 m / 4 500 m), simplify by dividing both by the numerator, and give the answer as 1 : 15, ideally with a one-sentence interpretation. Checks: sense (is the steepness plausible), reverse arithmetic (15 × 300 = 4 500), and units (both in metres before dividing).
